paragraphs.text: Theme 1: Residents need clear and accessible information about the water-distribution schedule.
Theme 2: Unexpected water-supply interruptions create a need for timely updates about water availability.
Theme 3: Residents need a clearer way to report pump-related problems and communicate concerns.

Residents of Purok 1, Barangay Kauswagan experience difficulty monitoring the community water supply because they encounter unexpected interruptions and have difficulty reporting pump-related problems, while concerns about the distribution schedule affect their awareness of water availability, resulting in uncertainty about water availability and difficulties communicating service issues.
Why This Problem Should Be Addressed
The issue should be examined because residents depend on the shared water-supply system, and clear updates and reporting can help them respond when service concerns arise.
Severity: Access to water is important for daily household activities. Unclear schedules or interruptions may disrupt residents' routines.
Frequency: The reported water-distribution schedule is from 7:00 AM to 8:30 AM. Unexpected interruptions sometimes occur, according to the information gathered during the interview.

Number of affected users: The shared water-supply system serves residents from purok 7 to Purok 1, Barangay Kauswagan. According to the interviewee, the water source also serves residents of Purok 7 in Barangay Polao and residents of Esobelle dormitory.
TubigTugon: Barangay Water Supply Monitoring and Information System
Why is this interface appropriate for the target users?
User characteristics: The residents are mostly senior citizen, aged 50, 66, 68 and 77. Use plain wording and readable text so the schedule is easy to check.
Accessibility: Residents can open the app on a phone or computer. Printed notices and direct announcements should remain available for households without reliable internet.

Ease of use: The first screen should show the water schedule and the latest service notice. A short report form can ask for the location, the problem and a contact method, with the resident's name optional.

Context of use: Residents can check the schedule before collecting water. The assigned representative can post changes with the date and time. An estimated return time should be shown only when confirmed.

Cagadas, Heart Q.  / Arapon, Geric / Angcog, Athea Jean P. / Gallego, Aljun / Chavez, Nathaniel / Sebusana, Marie Joy
Purok-1, Kauswagan, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental

Purok 1 is located in Barangay Kauswagan, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental. During the community observation, the residents were described as approachable and cooperative, with community members working together when concerns arise. The community has a shared water-supply system that uses a pump and communal water tanks locally known as pasong. During the visit, residents discussed the water-distribution schedule, unexpected interruptions, and difficulties in reporting pump-related problems. These concerns provide a basis for examining how water-supply information and community concerns are communicated. /
The residents of Purok 1, Barangay Kauswagan, including the residents interviewed.
Purok-1, Kauswagan, Tangub City, Misamis Occidental,

The observation focused on the community's shared water-supply system, which uses a pump and shared water tanks locally called pasong. Information was also gathered from residents about the water-distribution schedule, unexpected interruptions, and difficulties reporting pump problems.

The observation of the water tank (pasong) and the surrounding area was conducted in the morning by one of the group members and lasted approximately 20 minutes. The exact start and end times of the morning observation were not recorded. /  / The interview with the resident was conducted from 6:30 PM to 7:20 PM, lasting a total of 50 minutes. /  / Overall, the observation and interview activities took approximately 1 hour and 10 minutes, excluding travel time and other activities.

Describe how users interact with: / Other people: Residents discuss water schedules and interruptions. When water stops flowing, some residents need to approach the person controlling the supply; interview responses indicate that reporting a problem can be difficult. / Barangay services: The shared water system relies on a pump and communal pasong tanks. When the pump breaks, repairs may be costly and residents may need to contact the city. / Information systems: The available reports do not document an app, text-alert service, or centralized notification channel. Residents may not know when water will flow or return after an interruption. /

• Residents may not receive advance notice of interruptions or updates about when water service will return. / • Reporting pump-related problems can require contacting or visiting the person responsible, which residents describe as difficult. / • Pump repairs may be expensive and require contacting the city; the interview mentions that water can stop flowing for several days when the pump breaks. / • Uncertainty about the schedule and water availability can disrupt planning and may require residents to fetch water elsewhere.

Spoken notices are hard to review later. A written schedule gives residents a visible reference.
A kiosk needs equipment and a fixed location. Residents also need to check updates from home or work.
Automatic pump or flow sensors require added equipment and maintenance. The earlier findings focus on information and reporting needs.
